title: Music You Cannot Choose
sentences: For most of history, hearing music meant being present in the very room where it was played.
You listened to whatever the room around you happened to be playing.
Recording changed that completely, and the last twenty years have changed it again.
I can now hear almost any piece ever recorded within seconds of deciding to want it.
Curiously, my listening has narrowed over that same period rather than widening.
The system recommends whatever most closely resembles the things I have already liked.
The result is comfortable, very convenient and slightly airless.
I do still discover things, but the discoveries almost all feel quietly pre-approved.
The last piece that genuinely surprised me was played by a stranger in a station.
I would never have selected it myself, which is the entire point.
